copy.blurb:
FIFA World Cup 2026 on Sunday, overnight UTC kickoff, brings Australia and Türkiye together. The Desk's read disagrees with the market on the Australia side, by +13.8pp — and that disagreement is the Pick.

The Elo prior reads Australia 1740 vs Türkiye 1750: 10 points in favour of Türkiye, which is a meaningful but not decisive prior. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. No host, home-ground, or altitude adjustments apply here; the prior reads straight from Elo.

Three-way split from the model: Australia to win at 34%, the draw at 29%, and Türkiye to win at 36%. Each number is a probability over the full range of plausible in-form, no-injury, ninety-minute scenarios — not a prediction of a scoreline.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: Australia to win at 20%, the draw at 26%, and Türkiye to win at 54%. Reading those three numbers as a probability distribution, the market's view is internally consistent. The disagreement with the model is concentrated on the Australia side — 20% on the market, 34% on the engine, a +13.8pp gap.

Pick gate is a lower-bound check, not the point estimate. A 100-sample bootstrap perturbs the Elo prior (±20), the host bonus (±15), and the altitude bonus (±10), then reads the 5th-percentile probability back out. On the Australia side that lower bound is 30% — +9.0pp clear of the market's 20%, comfortably past our +3pp threshold. Calibration tracks the closing market on the bulk sample; selection — picking the single side where the gap is wide — is where the engine's edge has to come from. This verdict is a selection call on the Australia side.

The number above is the most recent read; it isn't frozen. With kickoff 23 days out, we're still on weekly refresh; the daily cadence picks up inside T-5d. Injury news, the actual XI, and weather conditions at kickoff all feed back into the prior when they land. We republish on every refresh. The Desk surfaces edge; what to do with that surface is a reader's call.
drivers: Pre-tournament Elo gives Australia a stronger prior than the Polymarket line implies.
The +13.8pp gap clears our 3 percentage point threshold for a Pick.
Calibration sits with the closing market across recent fixtures, so selection is the lever.
Late-binding signals — form, confirmed XI, weather — re-evaluate closer to kickoff.
copy.summary: The model thinks Australia are mispriced. Our number reads 34% on the home side; the market reads 20%. The +13.8pp gap is the Pick.
copy.title: Australia v Türkiye · the model leans Australia
